Comment: The 25-year interstate transmission charge waiver is a commendable and transformative step that will significantly reduce green hydrogen production costs.
Capital subsidy under the SIGHT scheme must be extended to smaller component manufacturers; current thresholds heavily favor large conglomerates.
The draft lacks strict water consumption guidelines; producing green hydrogen in arid regions could severely deplete local groundwater aquifers.
Single-window environmental clearance mechanism outlined in Section 4 is praiseworthy and will eliminate bureaucratic bottlenecks.
Mandating a 10% green hydrogen blend in steel plants within 18 months is unrealistic and unworkable given current electrolyzer supply shortages.
Clause 3.2 is vague regarding the certification mechanism for exported green ammonia. Clear international standards must be adopted.
We strongly welcome the proposed consumption subsidies for green ammonia in the urea manufacturing sector.
Public consultation timelines were too short; citizens living near proposed coastal green hydrogen hubs should be given adequate grievance redressal.
Allocating dedicated bunkering berths for green methanol and ammonia at major ports will create an excellent export ecosystem.
Clarity is desperately needed on long-term power banking terms; arbitrary state regulatory changes represent a severe investment risk.
Banking of renewable energy on an annual basis instead of monthly is crucial for the financial viability of hydrogen plants.
Filing monthly carbon intensity audits creates unnecessary bureaucratic friction for small pilot projects.
The proposed national R&D corpus of 400 crores is an encouraging initiative to foster indigenous membrane and catalyst technology.
Unrestricted open access without standby charges will impose an unfair financial burden on state electricity distribution companies.
Mandatory safety buffer zones around high-pressure liquid hydrogen storage tanks are absolutely essential and well-defined.
The fast-track sandbox for emerging solid oxide electrolyzer technology is a progressive and visionary move.
Dedicated pipeline infrastructure for hydrogen transport is completely ignored in the current draft policy.
Green certification must mandate 100% additionality in renewable generation so coal power is not indirectly consumed.
The 12-month commissioning timeline for electrolyzer manufacturing grants is overly tight and impractical.
Incentives for hydrogen fuel cell heavy commercial vehicles are commendable and will accelerate freight decarbonization.
Section 12 penalties for minor reporting delays are disproportionately harsh and punitive for early-stage operators.
Creating a domestic green hydrogen trading desk on existing energy exchanges is a brilliant and pragmatic proposal.
Local communities surrounding green hydrogen special zones must receive mandatory CSR benefits and clean water access.
The inter-ministerial task force is an efficient structure to harmonize state and central policies.
Customs duty exemptions on imported titanium mesh for PEM electrolyzers are urgently needed to maintain competitiveness.
Carbon accounting methodology should follow strict lifecycle emission metrics of less than 2 kg CO2 per kg H2.
Standard operating procedures for blending up to 10% hydrogen in existing natural gas grids are vague and require technical annexures.
The long-term fiscal stability clause gives deep confidence to global institutional investors.
We strongly support the establishment of National Skill Development Centers for hydrogen safety engineers.
Cross-subsidy surcharges must be permanently waived for dedicated hydrogen solar parks across all state jurisdictions.
